name: SIEM
certifications: Microsoft Certified: Security Operations Analyst Associate (SC-200)

beginner.summary: For system administrators, network engineers, junior SOC staff and developers who will build or run a SIEM and have not done so before. Covers what a SIEM does, a practice lab with Wazuh and Elastic Security, the main log sources (Windows Security and Sysmon, Linux auditd and syslog, cloud and SaaS audit logs), agents and forwarders, timestamps, parsing, the ECS, OCSF and CIM schemas, searching with KQL in Microsoft Sentinel and ES|QL in Elastic Security, a first scheduled detection, MITRE ATT&CK mapping, alerts and incidents, enrichment, dashboards, Wazuh rules and active response, ingestion cost and retention, and a capstone that monitors a small hybrid estate end to end.
prerequisites: Administers Windows or Linux machines: installing packages, managing services and reading log files
Understands TCP/IP basics: IP addresses, ports, DNS and the difference between TCP and UDP
Has a laptop with 16 GB RAM and Docker or a hypervisor, plus a free Azure subscription or Elastic Cloud trial for the hosted labs
outcomes: Collect Windows, Linux, network and cloud audit logs into a SIEM with agents or syslog and confirm each source is arriving
Parse and normalise raw events into ECS, OCSF or CIM fields and explain why consistent field names matter for detection
Search security data with KQL and ES|QL and write a scheduled detection rule mapped to a MITRE ATT&CK technique
Triage the resulting alerts, enrich them with lookups and present the monitoring picture on a dashboard within a retention and cost budget
